title: The day of the visit: she approves the brakes and declines the shock absorbers in the website chat; her thanks the next morning
demonstrates: A returning website visitor is the same contact, and the assistant remembers her name and number. It cannot see or change a repair order, so an approval is a hand-over, kind escalation. The junior operator confirms in four minutes with the price, the total and the pick-up time. The thanks next day reopens the chat she owns: the assistant drafts, she edits and resolves.

scenario.who_writes: The same customer, from work, after reading the estimate the shop e-mailed her.
scenario.wants: To say yes to the front brakes and no to the rear shock absorbers.
scenario.what_happens: The inspection found worn front pads and rotors and a seeping rear shock absorber. She writes her decision in a new website visit; the assistant hands it over; Maya confirms the work, the total and the time. She pays by card that afternoon. Next morning she writes her thanks; the chat reopens, Maya sends the edited draft and resolves.

why: The assistant repeats her decision back in plain words and confirms nothing it cannot see.
Maya answers what was asked and then what she will be asked next: the total and the time, and why the shock absorber can wait.
The thanks is a new session of a resolved chat: reopened, drafted for, sent edited, resolved again.
new_facts: The estimate reached her by e-mail from the shop system at about 10:05 on the day of the visit (rdunlap@inbox.example).
The car was ready by 3:00; the order was closed and paid at about 15:10.
The seeping shock absorber is the right rear one.
